verdict.rationale: Braintrust ships an official MCP server that lets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other MCP clients query production logs and run evals. It also has a REST API, defined by an OpenAPI spec, for programmatic access to projects, experiments and datasets, so agent-driven trace querying for debugging is clearly documented. However, the evidence never explicitly shows an agent querying metrics or reading back eval/experiment results through the MCP server or API; it only shows running evals and managing experiments. missing for 10: explicit documentation that agents can query metrics (latency/cost/score aggregates) and retrieve eval/experiment results via MCP or API, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven debugging via the MCP server.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent query my traces, metrics, and eval results through an API or MCP server to debug my app

citations.quote: Query production logs, author prompts and scorers, configure monitoring, and run evals from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, and any other MCP-compatible client.
Connect Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients to Braintrust. Query logs, author scorers, configure Topics, and run evals from your editor.
The Braintrust API allows you to interact with all aspects of the Braintrust platform programmatically.
Create and manage projects, experiments, and datasets; Log traces and metrics
browse and query logs, sync data, and manage functions without leaving your terminal
